texts.preamble: Nagasubramanian vs Deputy Superintendent Of Police on 30 October, 2015 Author: S.Vimala Bench: S.Vimala Before The Madurai Bench Of Madras High Court Dated : 30.10.2015 Coram The Hon'Ble Mrs.Justice S.Vimala Crl.R.C.(MD)No.314 of 2015 and M.P.(Md) No.1 of 2015 Nagasubramanian ... Petitioner/Petitioner/Accused -vs- Deputy Superintendent of Police, O/ o. The Deputy Superintendent of Police, Ambasamudram Sub Division, Tirunelveli District. ... Respondent/Respondent/Complainant Prayer: Criminal Revision Petition is filed under Sections 397 and 401 of the Criminal Procedure Code to call for the records relating to the order passed in Cr.M.P.No.594/2015 in S.C.No.58 of 2014 dated 20.05.2015 by the learned 2nd Additional District Sessions Court (Pcr), Tirunelveli and [LEAKAGE_MASK] the same by discharging him from the above case. !For petitioner : Mr.B.Nagasubramanian (Party-in-person) ^For Respondent : Mr.P.Kandasamy Govt. Advocate (Crl.Side) For Amicus Curiae : Mr.R.Anand :O R D E R
texts.facts: The petitioner filed a petition under Section 227 Cr.P.C., before the II Additional District Judge, Tirunelveli, (in S.C. No.58 of 2014) seeking discharge from the offences alleged against him. By the judgment dated 20.05.2015, the petition was dismissed. Challenging the same, this revision petition Nagasubramanian vs Deputy Superintendent Of Police on 30 October, 2015 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104118981/ 1 has been filed. 2. The petitioner herein is functioning as Food Safety Officer for the area of Ambasamudram Block in Tirunelveli District. He was appointed as Food Safety Officer in G.O.No.151(AB2) issued by the Health and Family Welfare Department, under Section 37 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006. A special training has been afforded to him towards functioning as Food Safety Officer. His duty and power is to inspect all food establishment in the said area and also to take food samples and forward the same to the Food Laboratory for analysis towards ensuring quality. 2.1. The defacto complainant one Mr.Arunachalam, S/o.Sudalaimadan, submitted an application on 23.03.2013 for registration of his tea and grocery shop, which is located at Mannarkoil Village in Ambasamudram Block. Based on the application, the petitioner herein inspected the shop and found that many food items stored for sale in the shop are against the provisions of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, Rules 2011 and Regulations 2001. Further, it was found that the shop has been constructed with thatched roof and the construction was an encroachment on the highway. Therefore, the petitioner advised him to correct the defect and also to get ?No Objection Certificate? from the department of Highways and the department of Fire Service. He was scolded in filthy and unparliamentary language by Arunachalam and his relatives. On the very same day, the petitioner gave a complaint to the Ambasamudram Police Station. The Police issued only the Receipt No.127/2013, but did not take any action. 2.2. The petitioner wanted the defects to be cured by issuing a notice dated 01.04.2013. Thereafter, there was no reply. He was summoned by the Inspector of Police on 13.04.2013 and in the presence of the Inspector, the Advocate of the defacto complainant asked the petitioner to withdraw the complaint. He was also threatened that if the complaint is not withdrawn, he has to face the case under the provisions of SC/ST (POA) Act. Again the petitioner preferred a complaint. As there was no action based upon the complaint, the complaint was sent by a registered post (as per Section 154(3) of Cr.P.C.) to the Superintendent of Police. 2.3. As there was no action even by the Superintendent of Police, the petitioner filed a petition before learned Judicial Magistrate, seeking a direction to the Inspector of Police (under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C.) to register the First Information Report. On direction by the Magistrate, a case was registered in Crime No.181 of 2013. 2.4. On 03.08.2013, the petitioner inspected A/M Sorimuthu Iyyanar Temple to inspect the shop, which was temporarily established for Aadi Amavasai function. 130 Kgs. of tea power in the shop of one Mr.S.Esakki, was suspected to be furious. When the petitioner attempted to seize it, Esakki created law and order problem. Then, he approached the Inspector and Deputy Superintendent of Police to give protection. The Deputy Superintendent of Police refused to give protection on the ground that the petitioner obtained direction under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C. before the Judicial Magistrate. Adding insult to injury, the Deputy Superintendent of Police directed the Inspector to register a case against the petitioner himself. With the assistance of the higher Police officials, i.e. the Superintendent of Police, the petitioner was able to seize the spurious tea dust and send the sample for analysis for assurance of its quality. The lab report proved that the tea dust is of Nagasubramanian vs Deputy Superintendent Of Police on 30 October, 2015 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104118981/ 2 substandard quality. 2.5. In respect of the attitude exhibited by the Deputy Superintendent of Police, a letter was sent by a registered post as well as by email on 04.08.2013 to the Superintendent of Police. 2.6. With the connivance of the Deputy Superintendent of Police and the Inspector, the defacto complainant has submitted a complaint under the SC/ST (POA) Act on 10.08.2013. That compelled the petitioner to obtain an anticipatory bail and thereafter, he surrendered before the II Additional District Judge and got himself released on bail. Thereafter, when the final report was filed against him, the petitioner filed an application for discharge. the documents relied upon by the accused are not germane for consideration at the time of discharge.

Under Clause-3(t), the Food Safety Officer means an officer appointed under Section 37. ?3(q) ?food safety? means assurance that food is acceptable for human consumption according to its intended use; Nagasubramanian vs Deputy Superintendent Of Police on 30 October, 2015 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104118981/ 4 3(r) ?food safety audit? means a systematic and functionally independent examination of food safety measures adopted by manufacturing units to determine whether such measures and related results meet with objectives of food safety and the claims made in that behalf; 10.2. Section 37 provides for appointment of Food Safety Officer and Section 38 provides for powers of the Food Safety Officer. ?37. Food Safety Officer. (1) The Commissioner of Food Safety shall, by notification, appoint such persons as he thinks fit, having the qualifications prescribed by the Central Government, as Food Safety Officers for such local areas as he may assign to them for the purpose of performing functions under this Act and the rules and regulations made thereunder. (2) The State Government may authorise any officer of the State Government having the qualifications prescribed under sub-section (1) to perform the functions of a Food Safety Officer within a specified jurisdiction. 38. Powers of Food Safety Officer. (1) The Food Safety Officer may ? (a) take a sample ? (i) of any food, or any substance, which appears to him to be intended for sale, or to have been sold for human consumption; or (ii) of any article of food or substance which is found by him on or in any such premises; which he has reason to believe that it may be required as evidence in proceedings under any of the provisions of this Act or of the regulations or orders made thereunder; or (b) seize any article of food which appears to the Food Safety Officer to be in contravention of this Act or the regulations made thereunder; and (c) keep it in the safe custody of the food business operator such article of food after taking a sample; and in both cases send the same for analysis to a Food Analyst for the local area within which such sample has been taken: Provided that where the Food Safety Officer keeps such article in the safe custody of the food business operator, he may require the food business operator to execute a bond for a sum of money equal to the value of such article with one or more sureties as the Food Safety Officer deems fit and the food business operator shall execute the bond accordingly. (2) The Food Safety Officer may enter and inspect any place where the article of food is manufactured, or stored for sale, or stored for the manufacture of any other article Nagasubramanian vs Deputy Superintendent Of Police on 30 October, 2015 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104118981/ 5 of food, or exposed or exhibited for sale and where any adulterant is manufactured or kept, and take samples of such articles of food or adulterant for analysis.? 10.3. The liability of the Food Safety Officer, in case of vexatious exercise of power and the protection to Safety Officer, in case false complaint is made against him, is provided under Section 39 and Section 88. 39. Liability of Food Safety Officer in certain cases. Any Food Safety Officer exercising powers under this Act or the rules and regulations made thereunder who ? (a) vexatiously and without any reasonable ground seizes any article of food or adulterant; or (b) commits any other act to the injury of any person without having reason to believe that such act is necessary for the execution of his duty. shall be guilty of an offence under this Act and shall be liable to a penalty which may extend to one lakh rupees: Provided that in case any false complaint is made against a Food Safety Officer and it is proved so, the complainant shall be guilty of an offence under this Act and shall be punishable with fine which shall not be less than fifty thousand rupees but may extend to one lakh rupees. 88. Protection of action taken in good faith. No suit, prosecution or other legal proceedings shall lie against the Central Government, the State Government, the Food Authority and other bodies constituted under this Act or any officer of the Central Government, the State Government or any member, officer or other employee of such Authority and bodies or any other officer acting under this Act for anything which is in good faith done or intended to be done under this Act or the rules or regulations made thereunder. 11. From Section 88, it is evident that the officer acting under this Act get the protection, provided that the act is done in good faith or intended to be done under this Act or the rules or regulations made thereunder. Therefore, when the petitioner is a Public servant and when the incident is said to have taken place in the course of discharge of his official duties, there can be no prosecution, unless sanction is obtained under Section 197 of Cr.P.C. The said provision reads as under: Nagasubramanian vs Deputy Superintendent Of Police on 30 October, 2015 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104118981/ 6 197. Prosecution of Judges and public servants. (1) When any person who is or was a Judge or Magistrate or a public servant not removable from his office save by or with the sanction of the Government is accused of any offence alleged to have been committed by him while acting or purporting to act in the discharge of his official duty, no Court shall take cognizance of such offence except with the previous sanction- (a) in the case of a person who is employed or, as the case may be, was at the time of commission of the alleged offence employed, in connection with the affairs of the Union, of the Central Government; (b) in the case of a person who is employed or, as the case may be, was at the time of commission of the alleged offence employed, in connection with the affairs of a State, of the State Government: 1 Provided that where the alleged offence was committed by a person referred to in clause (b) during the period while a Proclamation issued under clause (1) of article 356 of the Constitution was in force in a State, clause (b) will apply as if for the expression" State Government" occurring therein, the expression" Central Government" were substituted. (2) No Court shall take cognizance of any offence alleged to have been committed by any member of the Armed Forces of the Union while acting or purporting to act in the discharge of his official duty, except with the previous sanction of the Central Government. 3..........? 13. Explaining the necessity of protecting the public servant and discharging public duties from vexatious prosecution, the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India has made the following observation in the case of Inspector of Police and ors vs Battenapatka venkata Ratnam and ors, reported in [2015(5)SCALE253]. ? Public servants have, in fact, been treated as special category Under Section 197 Code of Criminal Procedure, to protect them from malicious or vexatious prosecution. Such protection from harassment is given in public interest; the same cannot be treated as shield to protect corrupt officials. In Subramanian Swamy v. Manmohan Singh and Anr.(2012) 3 SCC 64, at paragraph- 74, it has been held that the provisions dealing with Section 197 Code of Criminal Procedure must be construed in such a manner as to advance the cause of honesty, justice and good governance. To quote: 74. ...Public servants are treated as a special class of persons enjoying the said protection so that they can perform their duties without fear and favour and without threats of malicious prosecution. However, the said protection against malicious prosecution which was extended in public interest cannot become a shield to protect Nagasubramanian vs Deputy Superintendent Of Police on 30 October, 2015 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104118981/ 7 corrupt officials.
